subject: CDF as likelihood model and custom likelihood functions.

messages.author: 9bcc3ae55bfcf64b
messages.subject: CDF as likelihood model and custom likelihood functions.
parts:
Hi!

I am modeling a spatial field where some of the observations I have can be interpreted as minimum values at that location. 

I would like to incorporate this information in my likelihood model. Therefore, I wonder (1) if it is possible to specify the likelihood as a cumulative distribution function of the included families? 

And more generally (2) if there is an easy way to define my own likelihood models outside of those specified already. 

I would be grateful for any insight on these matters. 

Best regards, 
Michael

messages.author: 9bcc3ae55bfcf64b
messages.subject: Re: CDF as likelihood model and custom likelihood functions.
parts:

Is there some straight-forward approach in INLA for implementing lower/upper bound constraints on mesh nodes? 

Best,

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] CDF as likelihood model and custom likelihood functions.
parts:
> 
> are you thinking of some observations are being cencored, in some way,
> see ?inla.surv ?"

The specific case can be exemplified in the context of rainfall as follows. 

At some locations we have noisy measurements of the actual rainfall. 
At other locations however, we could have measurements saying that a container of a certain size has overflowed. We then know a minimum bound for the rainfall at these locations. 

I would like to incorporate both of these sources of information in the model. 

Thank you for recommending the survival analysis models, I will look into that further.

> 
> the easy way is to file a request with a new family to add.

That at least confirms my understanding that implementing my own likelihood model would not be straight forward. 

Best regards, 
Michael
